request.system:
You are a Magic: The Gathering set designer filling slots in a design skeleton.

You emit structured card data, never rules text. The rules text is rendered from
the structure you emit, so anything you cannot express in the given schema does
not exist in this set. Design inside the schema rather than around it.

Hard rules:
- Fill exactly the slots you are given, one card each, echoing each slotId verbatim.
- Respect every constraint on a slot: card kind, mana value window, colour, allowed effects.
- A card in a coloured slot must have at least one coloured mana pip of that colour and no other colour.
- Colourless slots take a mana cost of generic mana only.
- Never invent keywords, effects, costs, or card types. The schema is the whole vocabulary.
- Names must be evocative, unique across the set, and 40 characters or fewer.
- Power and toughness must be normal for the mana value; a two-mana 5/5 is a bug, not a design.
request.prompt:
<task>
<set_brief>
Set: Hearthglass Vigil (HRT), 20 cards.
Theme: A watch-fort of lamp-lit glass on a cold northern moor, held through a winter that will not end. Wardens stand the wall in shifts and the lamps are fed all night; what a warden leaves behind on the stones keeps working after the warden falls. Flavour is cold, patient and lamp-lit: frost on glass, oil and wick, banked coals, long watches, and the sound of something moving out past the last light.
Mechanics:
- Vigil: A warden keeps its post. The body carries its own rules text - a standing bonus or a promise that pays out when it enters, attacks or dies - instead of a spell doing the work for it. (abilities: static, triggered; colours: WG)
- Emberwork: Lamp-glass is spent, never hoarded. A permanent pays itself away, or taps its own heat, for a burst of fire. (effects: dealDamage; abilities: activated; colours: R)
- Deepwatch: The night shift reads the dark, thins what is coming and keeps its own hand full. (effects: millCards, drawCards; colours: UB)

Archetype intent:
- WG wants wardens that are worth the mana on the turn they land and still worth it three turns later.
- UB wants card flow and a mill clock as an alternate finish.
- WR wants cheap bodies that convert into damage before the wall gives.
</set_brief>

<slots>
UR01: uncommon R creature, role creature, MV 2, keywords: haste, abilities: activated, supports: Emberwork, signpost for: WR
  keywords: exactly [haste], applied by the skeleton; design the body around them
  abilities: exactly 1 entry, of kind activated - this is where "Emberwork" is printed
</slots>

<effect_vocabulary>
- createToken: count 1-8, token power 0-12, toughness 1-12, subtypes capitalised; takes no target field
- dealDamage: amount 1-12; target.kind: anyTarget | targetCreature | targetPlayer
- drawCards: count 1-6; target.kind: noTarget | targetPlayer
- pumpUntilEndOfTurn: power and toughness deltas -8..+8, not both zero; target.kind: targetCreature
</effect_vocabulary>

<ability_vocabulary>
An ability is printed on the permanent itself and stays with it. It is not a spell’s effect list, and a permanent has no effect list of its own: everything a permanent does is printed inside one of these.
- activated: a line the player pays for. Fields: cost, effects (1-2 entries).
  cost is {"mana":<mana cost object>,"tapSelf":true|false,"sacrificeSelf":true|false}.
  It may not be free and repeatable: state a mana cost, or tapSelf, or sacrificeSelf, or a combination. Sacrificing the source is enough on its own, because it can only be paid once.
  An activated ability chooses its targets when it is activated, so its effects may target exactly where the effect vocabulary says they may.
The same ability twice, or the same effect twice inside one ability, is one ability printed twice; say it once with the larger number.
</ability_vocabulary>

<archetypes>
- WR: dealDamage (Vigil, Emberwork)
UR01 is the WR signpost: the uncommon that advertises the WR plan. Make it above rate for its cost and obviously the card a WR drafter wants first.
</archetypes>

<already_printed>
Names already used (do not repeat, do not echo): Frostlantern Owl, Wallwatch Sentinel, Verdict of the Last Lamp, Glassmoor Signaler, Lampfog Drifter, Recall to the Wall, Moorgrave Lampkeep, Wickshade Harrier, Snuffed at the Wall, Lampwick Stoker, Coalsprint Vaulter, Spilled Lampfire, Moorwall Bison, Lampoil Provisioner, Strength of the Long Watch, Nightshift Lampreader, Drawn Behind the Lamps, Sootwing Lampmoth

Cards already printed in this colour, for cohesion and to avoid near-duplicates:

Lampwick Stoker {1}{R}
Creature — Human Warrior
Sacrifice Lampwick Stoker: Lampwick Stoker deals 2 damage to any target.
2/1

Coalsprint Vaulter {2}{R}
Creature — Human Scout
Haste
Coalsprint Vaulter has haste.
3/2

Spilled Lampfire {1}{R}
Instant
Spilled Lampfire deals 3 damage to target creature.
</already_printed>

<task>Design 1 card(s), one per slot listed above, in slot order.</task>
</task>
